author: ChatGPT
method: Individually authored, kit-specific objectives and test plans; not generic candidate-package assignments.

builds.name: Reference: Ranked support core
builds.goal: Reference for Blitzcrank: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ support players use most (2,448 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 58.9% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A catch initiator who pulls a target into close-range knockup and silence, with short speed bursts for approach. The current support provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Locket of the Iron Solari → Zeke's Convergence → Bandlepipes. Glacial Augment keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Boots of Swiftness, Celestial Opposition, Knight's Vow.
builds.summary: The proven support baseline: Locket of the Iron Solari → Zeke's Convergence → Bandlepipes, with Glacial Augment.
testPlan: Play it in support as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Locket of the Iron Solari → Zeke's Convergence → Bandlepipes) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 58.9% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Locket of the Iron Solari → Zeke's Convergence → Bandlepipes.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

builds.name: Damage interaction: AD Power Fist ceiling
builds.goal: Push one landed E attack against a champion as high as possible under finite, repeatable conditions.
builds.summary: 345 item AD, 100% item crit chance, armor penetration and one Spellblade: a single-E ceiling candidate.
builds.hypothesis: Power Fist's stored 200% total-AD scaling motivates stacking AD rather than defaulting to AP. These six items supply 345 AD, four 25%-crit items, 35% armor penetration and 28 lethality in the snapshot. Infinity Edge supplies the crit-damage modifier; Essence Reaver adds a separately measured Spellblade packet. First Strike tests the first-combat-hit window, not permanent amplification. Absolute Focus requires more than 70% health; Gathering Storm must use a fixed game time. This is a candidate for an unusually large punch, not a searched global maximum.
testPlan: Use champion targets at level 18 with fixed armor (test 50, 100 and 200), 3000 max HP, and explicitly recorded bonus HP. Minion/monster E damage is a different test.

First isolate E: let ordinary attacks, item actives and R lightning remain separate observations. Record the E attack, Spellblade and First Strike contributions rather than calling the entire combo E damage.
Verify E critical-strike behavior with and without Infinity Edge on the live patch. Do not apply a guessed crit multiplier to every damage packet.
Test First Strike ready with no prior enemy hit, then on cooldown. Keep health above 70% for Absolute Focus and fix Gathering Storm time at 30 minutes; repeat at zero earned time/stacks.

At matched gold compare the late Youmuu slot with Swifties for access, and Bloodthirster with fully transformed Muramana for total E-plus-proc damage. Record actual max mana, transformation and proc behavior; do not assume multiple Shock procs.
After dummy trials, test landing E against a moving champion without Q, and Q → E inside First Strike's three-second window. Compare successful-hit damage with failed access.
failureConditions: The live E/crit interaction differs from the proposed mechanism.
An opponent hits first and denies First Strike, or low health removes Absolute Focus.
Giving up permanent boots prevents the punch or causes death before it lands.
tradeoffs: No defensive slot and no support quest: this is a farmed-role/late-game laboratory route, not a support shopping list.
A large first punch can lose to durability or repeated casts over six to ten seconds.
Collector execute is an execute threshold, not extra E base damage; LDR bonus-health amplification depends on the target.
buyOrder: For a farmed-role experiment: Essence Reaver for an E-triggered Spellblade/mana checkpoint, then Infinity Edge; compare the order at matched gold.
Keep movement boots during the build. Complete crit/penetration for the target; try Bloodthirster for raw AD.
Only replace boots with Youmuu at the late six-item ceiling if W/active movement still lets you land the attack.
coverageNotes: No numerical Blitzcrank adapter exists. These are champion-specific research hypotheses to measure in game, not computed optimal builds.

Use the stored patch 26.20 source: E tooltip is 2 × total AD + 0.25 × AP before armor and separate attack/item/rune effects. Critical-strike and proc interactions are not certified by that tooltip alone.
Do not double Spellblade, Muramana, rune damage or other on-hit effects merely because Power Fist says double damage. Separate E attack damage from extra packets.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Mana-shield boxer
builds.goal: Trade the single-E ceiling for additional E knockups and survival against physical attack pressure.
builds.summary: Mana Barrier, Muramana and Navori turn actual attack uptime into a repeated-E experiment.
builds.hypothesis: Blitzcrank's Mana Barrier makes mana a durability variable as well as a resource. Muramana and Frozen Heart add mana; Frozen Heart addresses physical attack pressure. Trinity rewards an actual E/ability-to-attack cadence. Navori reduces remaining basic cooldowns on real attacks, so W attack speed and the E attack reset may buy another knockup sooner. Press the Attack is for the repeated attack sequence; it does not grant its full three-hit effect to an isolated opening E. This trades raw punch damage for contact, resource and repeated control.
testPlan: Use fully transformed Muramana with finite Tear progress recorded; compare before transformation at matched gold. Measure actual shield size with fixed mana state.
Compare normal attack → E reset → normal attack against E-only. Record Press the Attack activation and damage separately; never credit a pre-stacked proc to the first hit.
Over a ten-second duel, count attacks actually landed, E casts and time between knockups with Navori equipped and with a matched-cost replacement.
Test against a physical auto-attacker, then a magic-burst opponent. Record survival, shield timing, W expiry/self-slow and mana consumed.
Repeat with enemy movement and damage: no uninterrupted attacks means no assumed Navori cooldown reduction. Record both successful contact and disengagement.
failureConditions: The target kites W and escapes after the first E, leaving Navori without attacks.
Mana Barrier and Sterak shield overlap without preventing the death that matters.
Magic damage makes the Frozen Heart purchase ineffective.
tradeoffs: Lower AD and crit ceiling than the one-punch route; Navori is an attack-uptime purchase.
A farmed-role experiment; mana items and transformation timing can make the early lane weak.
Mana Barrier and Sterak are finite triggered shields, not permanent health or immunity.
buyOrder: Tear only if the lane can afford the delayed power; Trinity provides the first actual attack-trade checkpoint.
Finish Muramana transformation and Frozen Heart for a physical matchup. Test Navori before committing to the full route.
Sterak and boots protect contact; replace matchup defense when magic damage is the real threat.

builds.name: Experiment: Keep R ready, stack lightning
builds.goal: Test a different damage source: fast AP-enhanced attacks and delayed R lightning, then a timed R finisher.
builds.summary: Hail of Blades and W load lightning marks; delay the R active long enough to test their payoff.
builds.hypothesis: Static Field's source says attacks mark enemies for delayed lightning while R is available. Rather than instantly spending R, this route tests W plus Hail of Blades attacks and the E reset while the passive can operate, then times the active. Nashor supplies AP on-hit damage; Dusk and Dawn supplies Spellblade and a separately verified extra on-hit application. Q and R have strong AP ratios, but E remains physical with a smaller 25% AP contribution. Magic penetration helps magic packets, not the physical E. Whether marks coexist or refresh, and whether extra on-hit applications create extra marks, must be measured before crediting them.
testPlan: Start with R ready. Compare Q → normal attack → E reset → attacks → delayed R against Q → E → immediate R, at identical gold, ranks and health.
Record each real attack, each lightning mark and each delayed zap. Determine whether rapid marks stack or refresh, and what happens to pending marks when R is cast.
Isolate Dusk and Dawn plus Nashor: count the actual on-hit applications. Do not turn an extra item on-hit into another E knockup or R mark without observing it.
Repeat with Hail of Blades ready and on cooldown; log attack-reset behavior, W duration and the self-slow escape risk.
Compare a three-second pick and a ten-second fight against equal armor/MR, then high-MR targets. Record physical E damage separately from Q/R/item magic damage.
If holding R loses the pick to shields or an enemy cast, repeat with immediate R. Damage patience is not worth losing shield removal or silence.
failureConditions: Rapid attacks refresh a lightning mark instead of creating the assumed multiple zaps.
R must be spent immediately for shield removal or silence, removing the intended attack window.
Low durability or poor attack access prevents the extra attacks.
tradeoffs: Lower physical E ceiling than AD crit; this is an AP attack/lightning route.
Dusk/Nashor proc behavior remains a test, not multiplied damage granted by the tooltip.
Zhonya buys a survival window but also interrupts the attack cadence.
buyOrder: Nashor for the attack checkpoint; test Dusk and Dawn second with individual proc observations.
Deathcap/penetration are later choices; prioritize survival if another attack window is worth more.
Preserve appropriate boots and record finite Gathering Storm time and Ultimate Hunter takedowns.
